rows.Name: KB Architecture: Cached Context > RAG
rows.Description:
Phase 1 passes the processed, consolidated knowledge base (~34,000 tokens, question-and-answer format) directly into the virtual agent's context instead of using retrieval-augmented generation (data store + embeddings + search tool). Proposed by Adam Lahmadi (Onix); Mary Nelson (REI) recommended adopting in-context first and evaluating future expansion needs later.
Rationale: better performance on complex and multi-turn queries; faster and more accurate than RAG against Ian's golden set, especially ambiguous/stress questions; median latency 2.4s vs 3.8s for search; session billing covers in-context tokens with no per-query search fees.
Replaces: original design (KB in data store, embeddings, retrieval grounding).

rows.Name: KB Update Process: Pipeline + Human Approval
rows.Description: Knowledge base changes flow through a data-processing pipeline (monitor Gladly Answers content for changes, extract, process/consolidate, redeploy into agent context) with human approval before a new VA version is published. Automation scripts and documentation are to be shared with REI. Content is expected to change infrequently (roughly every couple of months). REI is expected to maintain the process after handoff because how context is written or updated can affect agent performance.

rows.Name: Agent Quality Evaluation Approach (Non-RAG)
rows.Description: Because the agent uses cached context rather than retrieval, RAG metrics (groundedness, context relevance, retrieval ranking scores) will not exist in test or production. Quality is assessed with (1) human review of full customer journeys, (2) a custom LLM-based evaluator that scores whole multi-turn conversations against REI business rules and detects hallucination, and (3) repeatable happy-path test cases in the agent platform rerun after each change. Evaluation must account for multi-turn journeys, not isolated answers.

rows.Name: Phase 1 Launch at Parity (Unauthenticated First)
rows.Description: Phase 1 launches at parity with the current Gladly chat: name/email collection, knowledge search and human handoff. Current Gladly chat gives generic answers and links - it does not return customer-specific balances, member numbers or order status. Personalized (authenticated) responses and a token-based sign-in flow are deferred to a later phase and are not a launch blocker. Handoff, escalation and transcript continuity take priority over personalized answers for launch. REI's authentication is managed by a shared platform, so the user object is a later-phase integration.

rows.Name: Remove Customer Lookup from Phase 1 Launch and QA
rows.Description: The customer-information lookup (email to membership number / order data through the data adapter) is removed from the Phase 1 launch and QA scope and retained for possible activation after authentication exists. Phase 1 must not return individual customer data without authentication. Supersedes in part the Phase 1 Scope decision (read-only fetch of member information and order status) and the idea of showing the 3-5 most recent orders.

rows.Name: Use Case 3 Pivot: Knowledge Base / Help Center
rows.Description: Phase 1 Use Case 3 is the knowledge base / help center Q&A experience rather than order modification. Combined with the existing Phase 1 read-only scope and Spanish out of scope, this sets the Phase 1 build sequence (KB first, then Use Cases 1 and 2).

rows.Name: Phase 1 Uses Native Gladly Widget
rows.Description:
Phase 1 uses the native Gladly-owned widget for the 10/15 launch. The virtual agent (GCX) provides conversation logic; Gladly handles display, routing and live-agent handoff, so the agent continues in the existing interface. The custom Onix widget (single front door with Shopping Agent) is deferred to a later phase.
Rationale: the custom option requires Gladly Custom Channels (not enabled; cost and operational impact not understood) and would force changes to operating procedures, inbox/channel handling and reporting plus a rebuild of REI's website widget and Tealium deployment - not achievable in one week.
Supersedes the 10/5 alignment to pursue the custom widget first with the Gladly widget as fallback.

rows.Name: Live-Agent Handoff: Content and Format
rows.Description: Handoff to a Gladly specialist sends a single payload with customer identification, a summary of the escalation reason and the full AI-customer transcript, so customers do not repeat themselves. The native Gladly transcript/layout is retained; an optional condensed agent summary (request, handoff reason, suggested next step) is added alongside it provided it does not affect the 10/15 timeline. Matching the existing agent format is preferred but must not block the timeline. REI judged the 10/2 demo sufficient for the immediate need.

rows.Name: Safety and Legal Guardrails: Mirror Ask REI
rows.Description: Safety/legal-related guardrails (e.g., self-harm, emergencies, injury or legal exposure) should reuse the behavior already in Ask REI so REI chatbots respond consistently (canned response where no human escalation exists). Items that are really product/sales questions escalate to a human. The guardrail document is to be reviewed line by line by REI (green = input, yellow = discuss, red = exclude).

rows.Name: Knowledge Source: Gladly Answers, No Web Search
rows.Description: KB content is pulled from the Gladly Answers API (Help Center audience) - the same source as REI's AI Search. The agent will not use web search (including domain-restricted REI.com search); giving Gladly's agent REI.com access previously produced chaotic answers. Tools and forms referenced in answers (delivery issues, price adjustment, order lookup) must be present in the knowledge content.

rows.Name: Data Residency and Conversation Storage
rows.Description: All GCP resources stay in US regions; REI's AWS data is not migrated to Google Cloud. AI-only conversation history is stored automatically in BigQuery; conversations handed to humans flow Gladly to Snowflake as today. Piping AI-only chats into Snowflake/VOC (or using Looker on BigQuery) is deferred beyond Phase 1. Consequence at launch: AI-only chats are absent from Snowflake and no CSAT survey is sent for them (same as today).

rows.Name: Test Strategy: Curated Golden Set and Baseline QA
rows.Description: Initial golden set is a lightweight, curated set of ~56 representative questions (reduced from ~250 candidates drawn from a ~1,500-record sample of reviewed Gladly chats), each with a customer question and passing response over 2-3 turns on the most probable path; no soft/hard-fail scenarios in the first pass. It is a starting point to expand. Because it is mostly happy-path, it is supplemented with ambiguous, confusing and production-derived queries, and manual QA (reviewer marks acceptable/unacceptable with reason) establishes the launch baseline before broader automation.
